title: Orbit and Protocol
premise: Petra Joubert, a clone of a murdered orbital magistrate, hauls freight along the Silence Corridor, the decommissioned jump route between two colonies that severed contact after an atrocity both governments erased. When a distress beacon transmits in a dead language only Petra's original could read, he is conscripted by both sides as a neutral courier and discovers the massacre never ended — it is being repeated, live, on the station where his original died. To prove it, Petra must recover his predecessor's hidden testimony from inside the station's sealed archive before the last jump window closes and the evidence burns with it. He succeeds at terrible cost, broadcasting the truth to both worlds, and chooses the ragtag crew who became his family over the duty that killed the man he was cloned from.
about_author: Theo Pemberton is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying traffic between ships that rarely spoke to each other directly. Orbit and Protocol is their third novel, written in port towns across three continents.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Petra runs the empty corridor between worlds Halcyon and Vesper, narrating his routine, his crew of misfits, and the ghost of his original's memories that surface unbidden. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; he insists he is content, and we see he isn't.

chapters.title: Dead Language, Live Signal
chapters.summary: A distress burst arrives in Old Meridian, extinct for two centuries — a language only the murdered magistrate Joubert Prime could read. Petra deciphers enough to know it names him. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: dread and fascination colliding; the past reaching through the dark to claim its copy.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Courier
chapters.summary: Both governments intercept Petra: Halcyon wants him to investigate quietly, Vesper wants him to confirm nothing happened. Each offers protection; each implies erasure if he refuses. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure — neutrality revealed as a trap with two doors.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Engineer Sefa, navigator Okonkwo, and medic Ilse debate whether to take the contract. Flashbacks show how each was discarded by one world or the other. They vote yes — for Petra, not the pay. POV: rotating crew. Emotional beat: found family solidifying around shared exile.

chapters.title: Approach Vector
chapters.summary: Transit toward Station Meridian, site of the original massacre and Joubert Prime's death. Petra experiences memory bleed — knowing corridors he has never walked. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: uncanny grief; mourning a man whose face is his own.

chapters.title: The Station That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Meridian appears derelict but its mass readings are wrong — something is hidden inside. First contact with survivors hiding in the old archive levels, speaking fragments of Old Meridian. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror as the 'derelict' breathes.

chapters.title: Testimony in Ash
chapters.summary: Survivor-archivist Nadege shows physical proof of ongoing purges: fresh scorch under decades-old dust. Every official record contradicts her. POV: Nadege. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by exhaustion — someone who has shouted into silence for years.

chapters.title: Protocol of Denial
chapters.summary: Halcyon's liaison, Commander Reyes, orders Petra to log the station as uninhabited. Petra stalls, discovering Reyes carries orders signed with Joubert Prime's posthumous authorization code. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: betrayal — his original's authority weaponized against the truth.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Memory bleed intensifies; Petra realizes his original hid testimony inside the archive's quantum core, encrypted in Old Meridian verse. He begins dreaming the hiding place. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: identity crisis — are these memories his inheritance or his leash?

chapters.title: Vesper's Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper agents board covertly, led by the charming, ruthless Adisa, who offers Petra citizenship, history, belonging — if he reports nothing. She reveals she knew Joubert Prime. POV: Adisa. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity; corruption offered as kindness.

chapters.title: Jump Window Mathematics
chapters.summary: Okonkwo calculates the corridor's final stable jump window: nineteen days, then the route closes for a decade. Everything must be decided inside that frame. POV: Okonkwo. Emotional beat: ticking-clock dread rendered as cold, beautiful numbers.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Petra, Nadege, and Sefa descend through flooded maintenance levels toward the quantum core, evading automated purge drones still executing century-old kill orders. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: terror and loyalty — she goes because leaving anyone behind is the one protocol she keeps.

chapters.title: Verse and Cipher
chapters.summary: At the core, Petra finds the encryption keyed to a poem only Joubert Prime wrote — and recites it from memory he shouldn't have. The archive opens. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: eerie communion with the dead; the clone completing the original's sentence.

chapters.title: The Massacre, Continued
chapters.summary: The testimony proves the purge never stopped: Vesper and Halcyon jointly cull survivors quarterly to keep the atrocity deniable. Current logs show the next cull in six days. POV: Nadege. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Reyes' Choice
chapters.summary: Petra confronts Reyes with the evidence. Torn between career and conscience, she reveals her own family died in the first massacre — and defects, giving Petra command codes. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the price of everything she was.

chapters.title: Betrayal Aboard
chapters.summary: Adisa seizes the ship while the away team is planet-side-adjacent, taking Okonkwo hostage and ordering the archive core thermally purged. POV: Okonkwo. Emotional beat: helpless rage; the family fractured from within.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: With hours left in the window, Petra trades himself to Adisa for Okonkwo and the core's survival, walking into custody carrying the full testimony in his own neural buffer. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love made structural.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: In Adisa's flagship brig, Petra hijacks the interrogation uplink and broadcasts the massacre record simultaneously to both worlds — the clone finishing what the original started, in the dead tongue and the living ones. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: catharsis; the silence finally broken.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: Both governments convulse: officers mutiny, publics riot, Adisa's command collapses as her own crews hear the broadcast. She faces Petra one last time — defeated, almost relieved. POV: Adisa. Emotional beat: tragedy recognized too late; power shown as a locked room.

chapters.title: The Last Window
chapters.summary: The crew makes the final jump window with refugees aboard as the corridor destabilizes behind them — the route that no longer speaks, closing forever. POV: Okonkwo. Emotional beat: bittersweet passage; leaving a grave and gaining a home.

chapters.title: Orbit and Protocol
chapters.summary: At the joint tribunal, Petra testifies as neither original nor copy but as himself. Justice is imperfect — some architects escape — but the record stands, unerasable now in ten million minds. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: sober triumph; truth as a foundation, not a victory.

chapters.title: New Heading
chapters.summary: Petra, Nadege, Reyes, and the crew launch a new route — unofficial, human, theirs. He visits Joubert Prime's memorial and speaks to the man whose life he inherited and outgrew. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: peace; the clone choosing his own orbit at last.
